claims.text: First: which contrast was used? Noncontrast: the preferred first study for urinary stones
claims.quote: Noncontrast CT is the preferred initial imaging study in most patients.

claims.text: IV contrast: improves imaging of tumors, infection, inflammation and trauma in soft tissues
claims.quote: To improve imaging of tumors, infection, inflammation, and trauma in soft tissues

claims.text: Oral (or rectal) contrast: helps separate the GI tract from the structures around it
claims.quote: Contrast in the GI tract helps distinguish the GI tract from surrounding structures.

claims.text: If perforation is suspected, oral contrast should be low-osmolar iodinated, not barium
claims.quote: Standard oral contrast is barium-based, but low-osmolar iodinated contrast should be used when intestinal perforation is suspected.

claims.text: Special studies CT urography: IV contrast is excreted into the collecting system, ureters and bladder, outlining the whole urinary tract
claims.quote: IV contrast concentrates in the kidneys and is excreted into the renal-collecting structures, ureters, and bladder.
claims.locator: Variations of CT, CT IV pyelography (CT IVP) or CT urography

claims.text: CT enterography: its unique advantage is identifying inflammatory bowel disease
claims.quote: The unique advantage of CT enterography is in: Identifying inflammatory bowel disease
claims.locator: Variations of CT, Virtual colonoscopy and CT enterography

claims.text: What to look for Stones: find the stone's location and how much it obstructs; also look for other causes of the pain, such as an aortic aneurysm
claims.quote: This study can detect the location of a calculus as well as the degree of obstruction. Moreover, CT may also reveal other causes of the pain (eg, aortic aneurysm).

claims.text: Appendix: contrast-enhanced CT diagnoses appendicitis accurately and can show other causes of an acute abdomen
claims.quote: Contrast-enhanced CT has good accuracy in diagnosing appendicitis (1) and can also reveal other causes of an acute abdomen.

claims.text: Radiation CT should use the lowest radiation dose possible
claims.quote: CT scanning should use the lowest radiation dose possible.
